+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Check that test files are wired into ("tethered to") the Buildkite CI.
+
+A test file is *tethered* when at least one Buildkite job actually collects it -
+some job's ``commands`` run ``pytest`` (or ``python`` / ``torchrun``, or a
+``find ... | xargs pytest`` pipeline) over a path that includes the file. A test
+that is collected by no job silently never runs: it passes review, merges, and
+rots.
+
+How it works
+------------
+1. Parse every job in every Buildkite pipeline yaml (and each ``mirror.amd``
+   sub-step), and turn each shell command into a :class:`Selection` describing
+   which test files it runs. The pipeline directories are read from
+   ``.buildkite/ci_config*.yaml`` (``job_dirs:``) - currently ``test_areas/``,
+   ``hardware_tests/`` and ``intel_jobs/`` across the CUDA, ROCm and Intel
+   pipelines - plus the legacy ``.buildkite/test-amd.yaml``.
+2. Build the inventory of test files under ``tests/``.
+3. A file is a problem if no selection runs it and it is not in the allowlist
+   (``tools/pre_commit/test_tethering_allowlist.txt`` - the set of pre-existing
+   gaps, which is only ever meant to shrink). Every allowlist entry must carry a
+   trailing ``# <reason>``; a bare path line is itself an error.
+
+Modes
+-----
+* **changed-files** (default): pre-commit passes the changed test files as
+  arguments; each one must be tethered or allowlisted.
+* **full scan**: ``--all``, or automatically whenever the change set touches a
+  pipeline yaml or the allowlist itself - because editing a job command can
+  orphan a test that is not otherwise in the diff. The full scan also reports
+  allowlist entries that have since become tethered, or whose file is gone, so
+  the list stays honest.
+
+Coverage from *any* of those pipelines counts - the question is "does some
+Buildkite job run this test", not "which pipeline". ``test-amd.yaml`` is being
+folded into ``test_areas/`` a group at a time; when it is gone the checker stops
+parsing it automatically.
+
+Usage::
+
+    python tools/pre_commit/check_test_tethering.py [FILES...]
+    python tools/pre_commit/check_test_tethering.py --all
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import fnmatch
+import shlex
+import subprocess
+import sys
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import regex as re
+import yaml
+
+REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
+BUILDKITE_DIR = REPO_ROOT / ".buildkite"
+# Fallback pipeline dir, always parsed even if ``ci_config*.yaml`` can't be read.
+TEST_AREAS_DIR = BUILDKITE_DIR / "test_areas"
+# The legacy hand-maintained AMD pipeline. It is being migrated into
+# ``test_areas/`` piecemeal; until that finishes, a test wired only into this
+# file is still genuinely run by CI, so it counts as tethered. When the file is
+# removed, ``_pipeline_yaml_paths()`` stops appending it automatically.
+TEST_AMD_YAML = BUILDKITE_DIR / "test-amd.yaml"
+TESTS_DIR = REPO_ROOT / "tests"
+ALLOWLIST_PATH = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "test_tethering_allowlist.txt"
+
+# `pytest` options that take a value in the *next* token, so that token must not
+# be mistaken for a test path (e.g. `-k expr`, `--shard-id 3`). Options that only
+# ever take their value with `=` (`--cov=...`) don't belong here - a bare
+# `--cov` takes no value and would wrongly swallow the following test path.
+PYTEST_OPTIONS_WITH_VALUE = {
+    "-k", "-m", "-p", "-n", "-c", "-o", "-W", "-r",
+    "--shard-id", "--num-shards", "--dist", "--durations", "--maxfail",
+    "--timeout", "--rootdir", "--junitxml", "--tb",
+}  # fmt: skip
+
+# `pytest` options whose value is a path that is *removed* from collection at
+# file granularity. ``--ignore`` takes a path prefix; ``--ignore-glob`` takes a
+# glob that pytest matches against the whole path with ``fnmatch`` (so its ``*``
+# *does* cross a ``/``), which is why the two are modelled separately.
+PYTEST_IGNORE_OPTIONS = {"--ignore", "--ignore-glob"}
+
+# `--deselect` takes a value too, but it removes individual node IDs - a file
+# with one parametrization deselected is still collected and still "run".
+PYTEST_DESELECT_OPTION = "--deselect"
+
+PYTEST_COMMANDS = {"pytest", "py.test"}
+
+# A leading ``$VAR/`` or ``${VAR}/`` path prefix - CI shell scripts routinely
+# name a test by an absolute path rooted at a shell var
+# (``"${GIT_ROOT}/tests/v1/..."``). The prefix is dropped before the path is
+# interpreted; an unresolved ``$`` anywhere else still makes the token unusable.
+_LEADING_VAR_PREFIX = re.compile(r"^\$\{?\w+\}?/")
+
+# Commands that execute a Python file directly. Only the *first* path argument is
+# the script that runs; everything after it is that script's own argv, not more
+# test files (``python tensorize.py --suffix v1`` runs one file, not ``tests/v1``).
+FILE_RUNNER_COMMANDS = {"python", "python3", "torchrun", "coverage"}
+
+
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
+# Shell-token helpers
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
+
+
+def _is_env_assignment(token: str) -> bool:
+    """True for a leading ``FOO=bar`` shell env-var assignment - the kind some
+    commands put before ``pytest`` (``VLLM_TEST_FORCE_LOAD_FORMAT=auto pytest``).
+    """
+    if "=" not in token:
+        return False
+    name = token.split("=", 1)[0]
+    return bool(name) and name.replace("_", "").isupper()
+
+
+def normalize_test_path(raw: str) -> str:
+    """Reduce a path as it appears in a command to one comparable form:
+    relative to ``tests/``, no surrounding quotes, no ``::nodeid`` selector, no
+    trailing slash.
+
+    Commands run from either the repo root or from ``tests/``, so both a
+    ``tests/`` and a ``/vllm-workspace/tests/`` prefix are stripped, as is a
+    leading ``$VAR/`` (``"${GIT_ROOT}/tests/..."``).
+    """
+    path = raw.strip().strip("'\"")
+    path = path.split("::", 1)[0]
+    path = _LEADING_VAR_PREFIX.sub("", path)
+    for prefix in ("./", "tests/", "/vllm-workspace/tests/"):
+        if path.startswith(prefix):
+            path = path[len(prefix) :]
+    return path.rstrip("/")
+
+
+def _token_is_test_path(token: str) -> bool:
+    """True if a shell token is a path argument rather than a flag, an env-var
+    assignment, a Buildkite ``$VAR``, or a ``-m`` / ``-k`` expression value.
+
+    A token with a ``/`` or a ``.py`` ending is always a path. A bare word
+    (``samplers``) only counts if it is really a directory under ``tests/``. A
+    leading ``$VAR/`` is dropped first, but a ``$`` anywhere else means the token
+    can't be resolved to a known path.
+    """
+    if not token or token.startswith("-"):
+        return False
+    if _is_env_assignment(token):
+        return False
+    token = _LEADING_VAR_PREFIX.sub("", token)
+    if "$" in token:
+        return False
+    if "/" in token or token.endswith(".py"):
+        return True
+    return (TESTS_DIR / normalize_test_path(token)).is_dir()
+
+
+def _path_is_within(parent: str, path: str) -> bool:
+    """True if ``path`` is ``parent`` itself or nested underneath it. A ``''`` /
+    ``'.'`` parent (a command run with no path arg) contains everything."""
+    if parent in ("", "."):
+        return True
+    return path == parent or path.startswith(parent + "/")
+
+
+def _glob_match_path(pattern: str, path: str) -> bool:
+    """Like :func:`fnmatch.fnmatch`, but ``*`` and ``?`` do not match across a
+    ``/`` - the way the shell and ``pytest`` treat an unexpanded glob path
+    argument (``kernels/test_foo_*.py`` selects one directory, not the tree).
+    A ``**`` component keeps the cross-separator meaning."""
+    if not any(ch in pattern for ch in "*?["):
+        return pattern == path
+    if "**" in pattern:
+        return fnmatch.fnmatch(path, pattern)
+    pattern_parts = pattern.split("/")
+    path_parts = path.split("/")
+    return len(pattern_parts) == len(path_parts) and all(
+        fnmatch.fnmatch(part, glob) for part, glob in zip(path_parts, pattern_parts)
+    )
+
+
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
+# Selections - "which test files does this command run?"
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
+
+
+@dataclass
+class PytestSelection:
+    """A ``pytest``-style command: run everything under ``included_paths``
+    except what an ``--ignore`` (path prefix) or ``--ignore-glob`` (whole-path
+    ``fnmatch``) removes."""
+
+    included_paths: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
+    ignored_paths: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
+    ignored_globs: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
+
+    def runs(self, test_file: str) -> bool:
+        included = any(self._arg_covers(arg, test_file) for arg in self.included_paths)
+        if not included:
+            return False
+        if any(self._arg_covers(arg, test_file) for arg in self.ignored_paths):
+            return False
+        # `--ignore-glob` is a plain `fnmatch` over the whole path - `*_tp.py`
+        # drops `kernels/nested/test_a_tp.py`, unlike a positional glob arg.
+        return not any(
+            fnmatch.fnmatch(test_file, normalize_test_path(glob))
+            for glob in self.ignored_globs
+        )
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _arg_covers(path_arg: str, test_file: str) -> bool:
+        """True if a single pytest path argument selects ``test_file`` - by
+        exact match, by being a parent directory, or as a glob."""
+        path_arg = normalize_test_path(path_arg)
+        if _path_is_within(path_arg, test_file):
+            return True
+        return _glob_match_path(path_arg, test_file)
+
+
+@dataclass
+class FindSelection:
+    """A ``find <root> -name ... [-not -name ...] [-maxdepth N] | xargs pytest``
+    pipeline. ``pytest`` runs one file per ``find`` hit, so the ``find``
+    expression alone defines the selected set."""
+
+    root: str
+    name_globs: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
+    exclude_name_globs: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
+    max_depth: int | None = None
+
+    def runs(self, test_file: str) -> bool:
+        root = normalize_test_path(self.root)
+        if not _path_is_within(root, test_file):
+            return False
+
+        # `find <root>` puts a direct child at depth 1, whether <root> is a real
+        # subdir ("compile") or the tests/ root itself ("" / ".").
+        below = test_file if root in ("", ".") else test_file[len(root) :]
+        depth_below_root = below.lstrip("/").count("/") + 1
+        if self.max_depth is not None and depth_below_root > self.max_depth:
+            return False
+
+        filename = test_file.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
+        if self.name_globs and not _glob_any(filename, self.name_globs):
+            return False
+        return not _glob_any(filename, self.exclude_name_globs)
+
+
+Selection = PytestSelection | FindSelection
+
+
+def _glob_any(name: str, globs: list[str]) -> bool:
+    return any(fnmatch.fnmatch(name, glob) for glob in globs)
+
+
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
+# Parsing CI commands into selections
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
+
+
+def _parse_pytest_command(tokens: list[str]) -> PytestSelection:
+    """Read a ``pytest ...`` invocation's tokens into a :class:`PytestSelection`.
+
+    Positional path args are the included paths; ``--ignore`` values (and a
+    bare-path ``--deselect``) are ignored paths, ``--ignore-glob`` values are
+    ignored globs. Value-taking options and their values, and every other flag,
+    are skipped. ``-k`` / ``-m`` filtering is intentionally *not* modelled - a
+    file that a marker expression narrows is still "run".
+    """
+    selection = PytestSelection()
+
+    # Advance past the pytest token itself (and any env-var / wrapper prefix).
+    tokens = iter(tokens)
+    for token in tokens:
+        if token in PYTEST_COMMANDS:
+            break
+
+    for token in tokens:
+        opt, eq, inline = token.partition("=")
+        if opt in PYTEST_IGNORE_OPTIONS:
+            value = inline if eq else next(tokens, "")
+            if opt == "--ignore-glob":
+                selection.ignored_globs.append(value)
+            else:
+                selection.ignored_paths.append(value)
+        elif opt == PYTEST_DESELECT_OPTION:
+            value = inline if eq else next(tokens, "")
+            # A `path::node_id` deselect leaves the file collected; only a
+            # bare-path deselect removes anything at file granularity.
+            if value and "::" not in value:
+                selection.ignored_paths.append(value)
+        elif token in PYTEST_OPTIONS_WITH_VALUE:
+            next(tokens, None)  # consume and discard the option's value
+        elif token.startswith("-"):
+            continue
+        elif _token_is_test_path(token):
+            selection.included_paths.append(token)
+
+    return selection
+
+
+def _parse_find_command(tokens: list[str]) -> FindSelection | None:
+    """Read a ``find <root> -name ...`` command's tokens into a
+    :class:`FindSelection`, or return ``None`` if there is no usable ``find``."""
+    if "find" not in tokens:
+        return None
+
+    root: str | None = None
+    name_globs: list[str] = []
+    exclude_name_globs: list[str] = []
+    max_depth: int | None = None
+
+    tokens = iter(tokens[tokens.index("find") + 1 :])
+    negated = False
+    for token in tokens:
+        if token in ("-not", "!"):
+            negated = True
+            continue
+        if token in ("-name", "-iname"):
+            glob = next(tokens, "").strip("'\"")
+            (exclude_name_globs if negated else name_globs).append(glob)
+        elif token == "-maxdepth":
+            depth = next(tokens, "")
+            max_depth = int(depth) if depth.isdigit() else None
+        elif (
+            root is None and not token.startswith("-") and token not in PYTEST_COMMANDS
+        ):
+            root = token
+        negated = False
+
+    if root is None:
+        return None
+    return FindSelection(root, name_globs, exclude_name_globs, max_depth)
+
+
+def _dash_c_code_operand(tokens: list[str]) -> str | None:
+    """For ``bash -c '<code>' [$0] [args]`` / ``sh -c ...`` / a combined short
+    group with ``c`` anywhere in it (``-ec``, ``-ce``, ``-euxc``), the ``<code>``
+    string the shell runs. ``None`` when this is not a ``-c`` invocation (plain
+    ``bash script.sh`` / ``bash -x script.sh``). Everything after the code
+    operand is a positional parameter (``$0``, ``$1``, ...), not a script or
+    command that executes."""
+    if not tokens or tokens[0].rsplit("/", 1)[-1] not in ("bash", "sh"):
+        return None
+    for i, token in enumerate(tokens[1:], start=1):
+        if not token.startswith("-"):
+            return None  # script operand reached; a later `-c` is *its* flag
+        # a short-option group (single dash) with `c` among its flags.
+        if not token.startswith("--") and "c" in token[1:]:
+            return tokens[i + 1] if i + 1 < len(tokens) else None
+    return None
+
+
+def _parse_shell_script(tokens: list[str], visited: set[str]) -> list[Selection]:
+    """Follow a ``bash tests/foo.sh`` command: read the script and parse the
+    pytest / runner lines inside it. ``visited`` stops a script that (directly or
+    otherwise) refers back to itself; nesting is one level deep in practice.
+    """
+    if _dash_c_code_operand(tokens) is not None:
+        return []  # the `-c` code string is parsed by the caller, not a file
+    script_arg = next((t for t in tokens if t.endswith(".sh")), None)
+    if script_arg is None:
+        return []
+
+    rel = script_arg.strip().strip("'\"").replace("/vllm-workspace/", "")
+    rel = rel.replace("vllm-workspace/", "").removeprefix("./").removeprefix("/")
+    candidates = [REPO_ROOT / rel, TESTS_DIR / normalize_test_path(rel)]
+    script_path = next((p for p in candidates if p.is_file()), None)
+    if script_path is None or str(script_path) in visited:
+        return []
+    visited.add(str(script_path))
+
+    # Join `\`-continued lines (a `pytest ... \` with its path on the next line
+    # is common), then track literal `VAR=value` assignments so a later
+    # `pytest "$VAR"` - the import-canary pattern - resolves to a real path.
+    text = script_path.read_text().replace("\\\n", " ")
+    var_values: dict[str, str] = {}
+    selections: list[Selection] = []
+    for line in text.splitlines():
+        line = line.strip()
+        if not line or line.startswith("#"):
+            continue
+        assignment = re.match(r"^(\w+)=(\S+)$", line)
+        if assignment:
+            var_values[assignment.group(1)] = assignment.group(2).strip("'\"")
+            continue
+        if var_values:
+            line = _expand_vars(line, var_values)
+        selections.extend(_parse_command(line, visited))
+    return selections
+
+
+def _expand_vars(line: str, var_values: dict[str, str]) -> str:
+    """Substitute known ``$VAR`` / ``${VAR}`` in a script line - but not inside
+    single quotes, where the shell does not expand (``pytest '$X'`` passes a
+    literal ``$X``, collecting nothing)."""
+
+    def sub(segment: str) -> str:
+        return re.sub(
+            r"\$\{(\w+)\}|\$(\w+)",
+            lambda m: var_values.get(m.group(1) or m.group(2), m.group(0)),
+            segment,
+        )
+
+    # Splitting on `'`: even-indexed segments are outside single quotes, odd are
+    # inside. (A `'` within double quotes splits wrongly, but that only ever
+    # drops a substitution - the safe direction.)
+    parts = line.split("'")
+    return "'".join(sub(p) if i % 2 == 0 else p for i, p in enumerate(parts))
+
+
+# Shell tokens (or runs of them) that separate one sub-command from the next.
+_SHELL_SEP_CHARS = set("|&;()<>")
+_RUNNER_KEYWORDS = PYTEST_COMMANDS | FILE_RUNNER_COMMANDS
+
+# Tokens that can precede the real command word without being it.
+_COMMAND_WRAPPERS = {"if", "!", "then", "time", "exec", "nice", "command", "builtin"}
+
+
+def _effective_command_index(tokens: list[str]) -> int:
+    """Index of the token that names the command actually executed, past leading
+    ``FOO=bar`` assignments and simple wrappers - ``if ! env FOO=1 bash x.sh``
+    resolves to the ``bash``, so ``echo x.sh`` stays ``echo`` and is not
+    followed. Returns ``len(tokens)`` when nothing executable is left."""
+    i = 0
+    while i < len(tokens):
+        token = tokens[i]
+        if _is_env_assignment(token) or token in _COMMAND_WRAPPERS:
+            i += 1
+        elif token == "env":
+            i += 1
+            while i < len(tokens) and (
+                _is_env_assignment(tokens[i]) or "$" in tokens[i] or tokens[i] == "-"
+            ):
+                i += 1
+        elif token == "timeout" and i + 1 < len(tokens):
+            i += 1
+            while i < len(tokens) and tokens[i].startswith("-"):
+                # `-k` / `--kill-after` / `-s` / `--signal` take a value.
+                if tokens[i] in ("-k", "--kill-after", "-s", "--signal"):
+                    i += 1
+                i += 1
+            i += 1  # the DURATION operand
+        else:
+            break
+    return i
+
+
+def _split_shell_stages(command: str) -> list[tuple[str, list[str]]]:
+    """Tokenize a shell line - honouring quotes - and split it at the shell
+    operators, tagging each stage with the operator token that *precedes* it
+    (``""`` for the first stage, then ``"|"`` / ``"&&"`` / ``"||"`` / ``";"`` /
+    ``"&"`` / a subshell paren). Knowing which operator joins two stages is what
+    lets a ``find`` sweep count only when it is genuinely piped into ``pytest``,
+    not merely on the same line as one. A line that cannot be tokenized
+    (unbalanced quote, ...) yields nothing: better to miss a selection than to
+    misparse one. Splitting *after* tokenizing means an operator inside a quoted
+    argument stays part of that argument."""
+    lexer = shlex.shlex(command, posix=True, punctuation_chars=True)
+    lexer.whitespace_split = True
+    try:
+        tokens = list(lexer)
+    except ValueError:
+        return []
+
+    stages: list[tuple[str, list[str]]] = [("", [])]
+    in_exec = False  # inside a `find -exec ... \;` action - its `;` terminates
+    for token in tokens:
+        if in_exec and token in (";", "+"):
+            stages[-1][1].append(token)
+            in_exec = False
+        elif token and set(token) <= _SHELL_SEP_CHARS:
+            stages.append((token, []))
+            in_exec = False
+        else:
+            stages[-1][1].append(token)
+            if token in ("-exec", "-execdir"):
+                in_exec = True
+    return [(sep, sub) for sep, sub in stages if sub]
+
+
+def _looks_like_command_string(token: str) -> bool:
+    """True for a single token that is itself a command line - e.g. a quoted
+    ``"pytest a.py && torchrun b.py"`` passed as an argument to a runner
+    script."""
+    return " " in token and any(word in _RUNNER_KEYWORDS for word in token.split())
+
+
+def _classify_subcommand(tokens: list[str], visited: set[str]) -> list[Selection]:
+    """Map one already-tokenized sub-command to the selections it implies:
+    find / pytest / ``bash <script>`` / direct file runner. Anything else
+    contributes nothing - better to miss a real selection than to invent
+    coverage that isn't there."""
+    if not tokens:
+        return []
+
+    is_find = "find" in tokens and any(t in ("-name", "-iname") for t in tokens)
+    if is_find:
+        find_selection = _parse_find_command(tokens)
+        return [find_selection] if find_selection is not None else []
+
+    # A `pytest` token only counts when `pytest` is the command that actually
+    # runs - `echo pytest kernels` prints text, it does not collect anything.
+    if _runs_pytest(tokens):
+        return [_parse_pytest_command(tokens)]
+
+    # Resolve the real command word past `FOO=1` / `env` / `if ! ...` wrappers,
+    # so `env FOO=1 bash x.sh` is followed but `echo x.sh` (Buildkite just
+    # printing a filename) is not.
+    cmd_index = _effective_command_index(tokens)
+    command_name = (
+        tokens[cmd_index].rsplit("/", 1)[-1] if cmd_index < len(tokens) else ""
+    )
+
+    if command_name in ("bash", "sh") or command_name.endswith(".sh"):
+        run_tokens = tokens[cmd_index:]
+        code = _dash_c_code_operand(run_tokens)
+        if code is not None:
+            # `bash -c '<code>' [$0] [args]` - only the `-c` string runs; the
+            # trailing args are positional params, not commands.
+            return _parse_command(code, visited)
+        selections = _parse_shell_script(run_tokens, visited)
+        # Runner scripts (run-multi-node-test.sh, ...) take the real test
+        # commands as quoted string arguments - parse those too.
+        for arg in run_tokens[1:]:
+            if _looks_like_command_string(arg):
+                selections.extend(_parse_command(arg, visited))
+        return selections
+
+    # `python` / `torchrun` / `coverage <file>.py`.
+    if command_name in FILE_RUNNER_COMMANDS:
+        rest = tokens[cmd_index + 1 :]
+        # `python -c '<code>' [argv...]` runs the code string, not a file - a
+        # later `-m pytest` or `.py` is that program's argv. Only honour a `-c`
+        # that is the interpreter's own (nothing script-like precedes it).
+        if "-c" in rest:
+            before_c = rest[: rest.index("-c")]
+            if "-m" not in before_c and not any(t.endswith(".py") for t in before_c):
+                return []
+        # `-m <module>` picks the module, not a script: only `-m pytest` runs
+        # tests. `python -m compileall kernels` collects nothing - the trailing
+        # `kernels` is compileall's argv, not a test path.
+        if "-m" in rest:
+            after_m = rest[rest.index("-m") + 1 :]
+            if after_m[:1] and after_m[0] in PYTEST_COMMANDS:
+                return [_parse_pytest_command(after_m)]
+            return []
+        # `python foo.py a b/c --suffix v1` executes only `foo.py`; the tokens
+        # after it are that script's argv - treating them as test paths tethers
+        # whatever directory an argument happens to name (`v1` -> `tests/v1`).
+        script = next(
+            (t for t in rest if t.endswith(".py") and _token_is_test_path(t)), None
+        )
+        if script is not None:
+            return [PytestSelection(included_paths=[script])]
+
+    return []
+
+
+# `xargs` options that consume the following token as their value.
+_XARGS_VALUE_FLAGS = {
+    "-n", "-L", "-P", "-s", "-I", "-i", "-J", "-E", "-d",
+    "--max-args", "--max-lines", "--max-procs", "--replace", "--delimiter",
+}  # fmt: skip
+
+
+def _xargs_command_tokens(tokens: list[str]) -> list[str]:
+    """The command (plus its args) that ``xargs`` will exec, with ``xargs``' own
+    options stripped: ``xargs -0 -n1 -I{} env FOO=1 pytest`` -> ``['env',
+    'FOO=1', 'pytest']``."""
+    i = 0
+    while i < len(tokens):
+        if tokens[i] in _XARGS_VALUE_FLAGS:
+            i += 2
+        elif tokens[i].startswith("-"):
+            i += 1
+        else:
+            return tokens[i:]
+    return []
+
+
+def _runs_pytest(tokens: list[str]) -> bool:
+    """True if ``tokens`` is a command that executes ``pytest``, seeing through
+    ``env FOO=1`` / ``timeout`` / ``if !`` wrappers (``xargs echo pytest`` is
+    not - ``echo`` is what runs)."""
+    idx = _effective_command_index(tokens)
+    return idx < len(tokens) and tokens[idx] in PYTEST_COMMANDS
+
+
+# Pipe stages that reorder or echo the stream without dropping any line, so
+# every `find` match still reaches a downstream `xargs pytest`. Anything else
+# (`head`, `grep`, `shuf`, `sed -n`, ...) filters, and then only some matches
+# run - not enough to claim the whole sweep is tethered.
+_PIPE_PASSTHROUGH = {"sort", "tee", "cat", "tac"}
+
+
+def _find_feeds_pytest(stages: list[tuple[str, list[str]]], find_index: int) -> bool:
+    """True if the ``find`` stage at ``find_index`` actually runs its matches
+    through ``pytest``: a *terminated* ``-exec pytest ... \\;`` / ``... +`` in the
+    ``find`` itself, or an ``xargs`` whose command operand is ``pytest``, reached
+    through ``|`` pipes of non-filtering stages only. A ``find`` piped to
+    ``wc`` / ``head`` / an ``xargs echo``, an unterminated ``-exec``, or a
+    ``pytest`` in a separate ``;`` / ``&&`` command, runs nothing (or not the
+    whole sweep)."""
+    find_tokens = stages[find_index][1]
+    for i, token in enumerate(find_tokens):
+        if token in ("-exec", "-execdir"):
+            action = find_tokens[i + 1 :]
+            if _exec_runs_matches_through_pytest(action):
+                return True
+    for sep, tokens in stages[find_index + 1 :]:
+        if sep != "|":
+            break
+        if tokens[:1] == ["xargs"] and _runs_pytest(_xargs_command_tokens(tokens[1:])):
+            return True
+        if tokens[:1] and tokens[0] in _PIPE_PASSTHROUGH:
+            continue
+        break
+    return False
+
+
+def _terminated(exec_action: list[str]) -> bool:
+    """A ``find -exec`` action only runs if it ends with a ``;`` or ``+`` token
+    (from ``\\;`` / ``+`` on the command line)."""
+    return ";" in exec_action or "+" in exec_action
+
+
+def _exec_runs_matches_through_pytest(action: list[str]) -> bool:
+    """True if a ``find -exec``/``-execdir`` action runs ``pytest`` over each
+    *matched* file: ``pytest`` is the command, the action is terminated
+    (``\\;`` / ``+``), and the ``{}`` placeholder lands as a positional test-path
+    argument - not as the value of an option (``-exec pytest --ignore {} \\;``
+    only ever runs whatever positional file is also on the line)."""
+    if not action or action[0] not in PYTEST_COMMANDS or not _terminated(action):
+        return False
+    # Substitute a real-looking path for `{}` and see whether pytest's own arg
+    # parser keeps it as an included path rather than eating it as an option value.
+    probe = [t.replace("{}", "_find_match_.py") for t in action[:-1]]
+    selection = _parse_pytest_command(probe)
+    return any("_find_match_" in path for path in selection.included_paths)
+
+
+def _parse_command(command: str, visited: set[str] | None = None) -> list[Selection]:
+    """Turn one yaml ``commands:`` entry into the selections it implies.
+
+    The line is tokenized (respecting quotes) and split into stages at the shell
+    operators, and each stage is classified independently so that, e.g., a
+    ``find`` and a ``pytest`` on the same line are both handled. A ``find -name``
+    sweep is kept only when :func:`_find_feeds_pytest` confirms its output
+    actually reaches ``pytest`` - otherwise it would invent coverage.
+    """
+    visited = visited if visited is not None else set()
+    stages = _split_shell_stages(command)
+    selections: list[Selection] = []
+    for index, (_, tokens) in enumerate(stages):
+        for selection in _classify_subcommand(tokens, visited):
+            if isinstance(selection, FindSelection) and not _find_feeds_pytest(
+                stages, index
+            ):
+                continue
+            selections.append(selection)
+    return selections
+
+
+def _iter_job_steps(yaml_doc: dict):
+    """Yield each job step in a test_areas yaml, plus a merged view of each
+    ``mirror.*`` sub-step. The AMD mirror can override ``commands``, so it has to
+    be checked as its own step."""
+    for step in yaml_doc.get("steps") or []:
+        if not isinstance(step, dict):
+            continue
+        yield step
+
+        for mirror_step in (step.get("mirror") or {}).values():
+            if isinstance(mirror_step, dict):
+                merged = {**step, **mirror_step}
+                merged.pop("mirror", None)
+                yield merged
+
+
+def _pipeline_job_dirs() -> list[Path]:
+    """The Buildkite job directories, read from every ``.buildkite/ci_config*.yaml``
+    (``job_dirs:``). Buildkite itself uses these files to assemble each pipeline,
+    so a test wired into any job under any of them is genuinely run by CI. Falls
+    back to ``test_areas/`` alone if no config is readable."""
+    job_dirs: set[Path] = {TEST_AREAS_DIR}
+    for config in sorted((REPO_ROOT / ".buildkite").glob("ci_config*.yaml")):
+        try:
+            doc = yaml.safe_load(config.read_text()) or {}
+        except yaml.YAMLError:
+            continue
+        for rel in doc.get("job_dirs") or []:
+            job_dirs.add(REPO_ROOT / rel)
+    return sorted(job_dirs)
+
+
+def _pipeline_yaml_paths() -> list[Path]:
+    """Every Buildkite pipeline yaml whose jobs count as CI coverage: the yamls
+    in every :func:`_pipeline_job_dirs` directory plus the legacy ``test-amd.yaml``
+    (see ``TEST_AMD_YAML``)."""
+    paths: list[Path] = []
+    for job_dir in _pipeline_job_dirs():
+        paths.extend(sorted(job_dir.glob("*.yaml")))
+    if TEST_AMD_YAML.is_file():
+        paths.append(TEST_AMD_YAML)
+    return paths
+
+
+def load_selections() -> list[Selection]:
+    """Parse every CI pipeline yaml into the full list of selections - the CI's
+    complete picture of which test files it runs.
+
+    A yaml that doesn't parse is fatal: silently skipping it would drop whatever
+    coverage it defines and produce false "untethered" reports.
+    """
+    selections: list[Selection] = []
+    for yaml_path in _pipeline_yaml_paths():
+        try:
+            yaml_doc = yaml.safe_load(yaml_path.read_text()) or {}
+        except yaml.YAMLError as e:
+            rel = yaml_path.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)
+            raise SystemExit(f"error: {rel} is not valid YAML: {e}") from None
+        if not isinstance(yaml_doc, dict):
+            rel = yaml_path.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)
+            raise SystemExit(
+                f"error: {rel} is not a Buildkite pipeline "
+                f"(top-level {type(yaml_doc).__name__}, expected a mapping)"
+            )
+        for step in _iter_job_steps(yaml_doc):
+            commands = list(step.get("commands") or [])
+            if step.get("command"):  # some steps use the singular form
+                commands.append(step["command"])
+            for command in commands:
+                if isinstance(command, str):
+                    selections.extend(_parse_command(command))
+    return selections
+
+
+def is_tethered(test_file: str, selections: list[Selection]) -> bool:
+    """True if any CI selection runs ``test_file`` (path relative to ``tests/``
+    or to the repo root - both are accepted)."""
+    normalized = normalize_test_path(test_file)
+    return any(selection.runs(normalized) for selection in selections)
+
+
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
+# Test-file inventory and allowlist
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
+
+
+def is_test_module(repo_path: str) -> bool:
+    """True if ``repo_path`` is a pytest test module CI is expected to run - a
+    ``tests/**/test_*.py`` or ``*_test.py``, but not ``conftest.py`` /
+    ``__init__.py`` or other helper modules."""
+    if not repo_path.startswith("tests/") or not repo_path.endswith(".py"):
+        return False
+    filename = repo_path.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
+    if filename in ("conftest.py", "__init__.py"):
+        return False
+    return filename.startswith("test_") or filename.endswith("_test.py")
+
+
+def all_test_modules() -> list[str]:
+    """Every test module under ``tests/``, sorted. Prefers ``git ls-files`` so a
+    developer's local scratch files are never flagged; falls back to a
+    filesystem walk when run outside a git checkout - the CI test images bake in
+    ``tests/`` with no ``.git``, and there are no untracked scratch files there.
+    """
+    try:
+        tracked = subprocess.run(
+            ["git", "-C", str(REPO_ROOT), "ls-files", "tests/"],
+            capture_output=True,
+            text=True,
+            check=True,
+        ).stdout
+        paths = tracked.splitlines()
+    except (OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError):
+        paths = [p.relative_to(REPO_ROOT).as_posix() for p in TESTS_DIR.rglob("*.py")]
+    return sorted(path for path in paths if is_test_module(path))
+
+
+def load_allowlist() -> set[str]:
+    """Read the allowlist file into a set of repo-relative paths. Blank lines and
+    ``#`` comments (whole-line or trailing) are ignored."""
+    if not ALLOWLIST_PATH.exists():
+        return set()
+
+    paths = set()
+    for line in ALLOWLIST_PATH.read_text().splitlines():
+        path = line.split("#", 1)[0].strip()
+        if path:
+            paths.add(path)
+    return paths
+
+
+def allowlist_entries_missing_reason() -> list[str]:
+    """Allowlist paths with no trailing ``# reason`` on their own line. Every gap
+    has to say why the test can't be wired into a job, so a bare ``path`` line
+    (the easy way to silence the gate) is itself an error."""
+    if not ALLOWLIST_PATH.exists():
+        return []
+
+    offenders = []
+    for line in ALLOWLIST_PATH.read_text().splitlines():
+        path, _, comment = line.partition("#")
+        if path.strip() and not comment.strip():
+            offenders.append(path.strip())
+    return offenders
+
+
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
+# The two check modes
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
+
+
+def run_full_scan(
+    selections: list[Selection], allowlist: set[str], *, strict: bool
+) -> int:
+    """Scan every test module. Untethered files that aren't allowlisted are
+    always errors. Allowlist entries that have become tethered, or whose file no
+    longer exists, are reported either way but are only errors when ``strict``
+    (an explicit ``--all`` run, as opposed to a PR that happened to touch CI
+    config - which shouldn't be blocked by unrelated allowlist cleanup).
+    """
+    untethered = [
+        path
+        for path in all_test_modules()
+        if path not in allowlist and not is_tethered(path, selections)
+    ]
+    now_tethered = sorted(path for path in allowlist if is_tethered(path, selections))
+    deleted = sorted(path for path in allowlist if not (REPO_ROOT / path).exists())
+
+    for path in untethered:
+        print(f"error: {path} is not run by any Buildkite job")
+    for path in now_tethered:
+        print(f"note: {path} is now tethered - remove it from the allowlist")
+    for path in deleted:
+        print(f"note: {path} no longer exists - remove it from the allowlist")
+
+    if untethered:
+        print(
+            f"\n{len(untethered)} test file(s) exist but run in no CI job. Wire "
+            "each into a job's `commands` in a .buildkite/ pipeline yaml, or add "
+            f"it to {ALLOWLIST_PATH.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)} with a reason."
+        )
+
+    error_count = len(untethered)
+    if strict:
+        error_count += len(now_tethered) + len(deleted)
+    return 1 if error_count else 0
+
+
+def run_changed_files_check(
+    paths: list[str], selections: list[Selection], allowlist: set[str]
+) -> int:
+    """Check only the given paths (what pre-commit passes). Non-test files, and
+    paths that don't exist on disk, are ignored."""
+    untethered = []
+    for raw_path in paths:
+        repo_path = _to_repo_relative(raw_path)
+        if not is_test_module(repo_path) or not (REPO_ROOT / repo_path).is_file():
+            continue
+        if repo_path in allowlist or is_tethered(repo_path, selections):
+            continue
+        untethered.append(repo_path)
+
+    for path in untethered:
+        print(f"error: {path} is not run by any Buildkite job")
+    if untethered:
+        print(
+            "\nAdd the test to a job's `commands` (and `source_file_dependencies`)"
+            " in a .buildkite/ pipeline yaml, or, if it is intentionally not run "
+            f"in CI, add it to {ALLOWLIST_PATH.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)} with a "
+            "comment explaining why."
+        )
+    return 1 if untethered else 0
+
+
+def _to_repo_relative(path: str) -> str:
+    if Path(path).is_absolute():
+        path = str(Path(path).resolve().relative_to(REPO_ROOT))
+    return path.replace("\\", "/")
+
+
+def _change_set_touches_ci_config(paths: list[str]) -> bool:
+    """A change to a pipeline yaml, a ci_config, or the allowlist can orphan a
+    test that is not itself in the change set, so those changes force a full
+    scan."""
+    return any(
+        ".buildkite/test_areas/" in path
+        or ".buildkite/hardware_tests/" in path
+        or ".buildkite/intel_jobs/" in path
+        or ".buildkite/ci_config" in path
+        or path.endswith("test-amd.yaml")
+        or path.endswith("test_tethering_allowlist.txt")
+        for path in paths
+    )
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("files", nargs="*", help="test files to check")
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--all", action="store_true", help="scan every test file in the tree"
+    )
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+
+    selections = load_selections()
+    allowlist = load_allowlist()
+
+    unreasoned = allowlist_entries_missing_reason()
+    for path in unreasoned:
+        print(
+            f"error: {ALLOWLIST_PATH.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)}: {path} has no "
+            "trailing '# <reason>' - say why it can't be wired into a job"
+        )
+
+    if args.all or _change_set_touches_ci_config(args.files):
+        rc = run_full_scan(selections, allowlist, strict=args.all)
+    else:
+        rc = run_changed_files_check(args.files, selections, allowlist)
+    return 1 if (unreasoned or rc) else 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())

[Docker] Expose bundled vllm-rs on PATH (#57606)

## Purpose

Expose the existing `vllm-rs` executable on `PATH` in the CUDA serving image. The wheel already bundles it inside the `vllm` package, but installing the wheel only creates the Python `vllm` console script. This prevents calling `vllm-rs` from a container shell or selecting it with `--entrypoint vllm-rs`.

After installing the wheel, `vllm-base` links the bundled binary into `/usr/local/bin` and runs `vllm-rs --help` to check the executable at image-build time. The package location comes from Python's `sysconfig`, so it follows the selected Python version. The serving images inherit the link. The default `vllm serve` entrypoint is preserved.

Checked the published linux/amd64 tags on 2026-09-18:

| Tag | Build | Manifest digest |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `latest` | `v0.29.0` / `98dff2a81d74` | `sha256:082ca6f035279109041ffd3fe0695cb568b29bc580b35c4f297a66a08b216c1b` |
| `nightly` | `0.29.1rc1.dev347+gdee37d891` | `sha256:b88541ab10490f6ee43d2e352edcfcb4b4e0e6b1fdd26ed427c89d73e3fa6a7b` |

In both published containers, the bundled executable is `/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/vllm-rs` and works when invoked by its full path. Bare `vllm-rs --help` and `docker run --entrypoint vllm-rs ... --help` both fail with exit status 127.

Duplicate-work checks: searched open PRs for `"vllm-rs" "PATH"`, `"vllm-rs" "symlink"`, and `"vllm-rs" "entrypoint"`. No open PR addresses this change. #51503 adds a separate standalone renderer image; this fixes the existing CUDA serving image.

AI assistance was used to prepare this change.

## Test Plan

For each pinned image above, build a small validation image with `FROM <published-image>` and the exact new `RUN` instruction extracted from this Dockerfile. Run these checks against the resulting image (`$patched_image`):

```bash
docker run --rm --network none --entrypoint /bin/sh "$patched_image" \
  -c 'set -e; command -v vllm-rs; readlink /usr/local/bin/vllm-rs; vllm-rs --version; vllm-rs --help'
docker run --rm --network none --entrypoint vllm-rs "$patched_image" --help
docker run --rm --network none --user 2000:0 --entrypoint vllm-rs "$patched_image" --help
```

## Test Result

- Reproduced the missing command and Docker entrypoint failure on both unmodified published images: exit status 127.
- Built the validation layer on both images with `docker build --network none --build-arg BASE_IMAGE=<pinned-image> ...`: passed, including the new build-time `vllm-rs --help` check.
- All three runtime checks above passed for both patched images. `command -v vllm-rs` returns `/usr/local/bin/vllm-rs`, linked to the original bundled binary. Tested linux/amd64 without GPUs.

[Fast Start] Cache the MTP draft model in a separate daemon group (#57312)




## Purpose

Under `--load-format ipc_cache`, the MTP draft model was not served by the weight cache daemon: the engine either reloaded it from disk or sent it to the target daemon with a mismatching fingerprint.

The launcher now starts a second daemon group for the MTP draft, with its own cache key, sockets (`*_draft0.sock`) and rendezvous port (`--weight-cache-draft-master-port`). On the engine side, get_draft_load_config routes an MTP draft to that group and lets other draft types (EAGLE3, DFlash, DSpark) fall back to disk. Only MTP drafts are cached; the draft must use the target's TP size.

diff --git a/vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/utils.py b/vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/utils.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000..1abbf572f8475d7f70e9743becc51a3b835ff246
--- /dev/null
+++ b/vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/utils.py
@@ -0,0 +1,48 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Helpers shared by the weight cache daemon, the IPC loader and the engine.
+
+These live outside ``protocol`` so callers that only need to know whether a
+draft is cached, or how a daemon group is named, do not have to import the
+wire format.
+"""
+
+from typing import Any
+
+from vllm.config import SpeculativeConfig
+from vllm.model_executor.models.interfaces import SupportsEagleBase
+
+# Speculative methods whose draft model the daemon caches in its own group.
+# Other drafts keep loading from disk in the engine.
+WEIGHT_CACHE_DRAFT_METHODS = frozenset({"mtp", "eagle", "eagle3"})
+
+# Python-side flags that weight loading sets on EAGLE-style drafts; the engine
+# never runs load_weights for cached models, so the daemon ships them.
+EXPORTED_MODEL_ATTRS = tuple(SupportsEagleBase.__annotations__)
+
+
+def export_model_attrs(model: Any) -> dict[str, bool]:
+    return {
+        name: bool(getattr(model, name))
+        for name in EXPORTED_MODEL_ATTRS
+        if hasattr(model, name)
+    }
+
+
+def is_draft_model_cacheable(speculative_config: SpeculativeConfig | None) -> bool:
+    """Whether the daemon serves the speculative draft as a separate role."""
+    return (
+        speculative_config is not None
+        and speculative_config.method in WEIGHT_CACHE_DRAFT_METHODS
+        and speculative_config.draft_model_config is not None
+    )
+
+
+def format_daemon_role(is_draft: bool) -> str:
+    """Name of a daemon group: the target model or the draft."""
+    return "draft" if is_draft else "target"
+
+
+def format_socket_role_suffix(is_draft: bool) -> str:
+    """Socket-name suffix keeping the draft group distinct from the target."""
+    return "_draft" if is_draft else ""

[Rust Frontend] Add MiMo V2.6 parser support (#57933)

## Purpose

Add MiMo V2 reasoning and tool-call support to the Rust frontend, including automatic parser selection for `mimo-v2` model IDs and explicit `mimo` parser selection.

- Alias the bare-delimiter reasoning parser to preserve whitespace around `<think>` / `</think>`.
- Reuse the Qwen Coder parser for `<function=...>` / `<parameter=...>` calls, with MiMo's bare tool boundaries and preserved parameter newlines.
- Normalize template-emitted `None` according to the parameter schema, preserving literal strings.
- Forward `parallel_tool_calls` to structural-tag construction, with a shared regression test.
- Keep standalone HF template discovery at the model root so auxiliary tokenizer templates cannot override the main tokenizer configuration.
- Add streaming parser coverage and a real-template roundtrip fixture for `XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL`.

Related to #44280. Existing proposals #49578 and #54393 register the Qwen3 reasoning parser and the JSON-based `Qwen3XmlToolParser`, respectively. This implementation uses bare reasoning delimiters and the function/parameter-tag grammar required by the published MiMo V2 templates, with whitespace preservation and template roundtrip coverage.

## Test Plan

From `rust/`:

```bash
cargo nextest run -p vllm-parser -p vllm-chat -p vllm-text --lib
cargo nextest run -p vllm-chat --test roundtrip -E 'test(roundtrip_mimo_v26)'
cargo clippy -p vllm-parser -p vllm-chat -p vllm-text --tests -- -D warnings
```

Run pre-commit hooks on the changed files.

## Test Result

- 911 library tests passed; 1 skipped.
- Reproduced the previous CI failure from an empty HF cache: the downloader selected `audio_tokenizer/chat_template.jinja`. The same MiMo V2.5 roundtrip passes from an empty cache after the template-discovery fix.
- MiMo V2.6 Flash roundtrip passed from an empty HF cache using the published tokenizer and chat template, covering reasoning enabled/disabled/default and mixed tool calls.
- Reviewed the published MiMo V2.6 metadata: Flash/Pro keep the bare reasoning and function/parameter-tag protocol; their new templates emit JSON scalars and omit inter-tag newlines, which the existing parser handles.
- Clippy and pre-commit passed.
- GPU generation and model-quality evaluation remain pending; validation covers parser behavior and template roundtrips.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation and validation.

[Bugfix][Spec Decode] Cap DFlash/DSpark profiling query batch (#56448)

Fixes #56443.

## Root Cause
The memory-profiling dummy run can hand-build max_num_seqs requests without applying the scheduler's speculative query-token budget. For DSpark/DFlash, each request can require num_query_per_req draft query rows.
For example, with max_num_seqs=512, max_num_batched_tokens=2048, and DSpark K=5, the profiling path asks the speculator for 512 * 5 = 2560 query rows while its input buffers are sized for 2048 rows, so DSpark can read _anchor_idx past input_ids and later surface CUDA IndexKernel/device-side assert errors.

## Changes
Cap the initial dummy/profile draft-generation pass to the largest complete set of query blocks that fits the speculator input buffer, preserve the full target-context and sampler projection for memory profiling, and fail early with a clear ValueError if a real query batch exceeds the input buffer.

Other profiling dummy runs, including FlashInfer autotune, build target attention metadata and cannot use the initial skip-attention shortcut. Add a default no-op speculator hook that lets DFlash-family speculators cap the dummy request count before GPUModelRunner builds those synthetic batches. This does not affect real serving requests or other speculator implementations.

## Existing PRs

#53970 addresses the same `max_num_seqs * parallel-draft query width > max_num_batched_tokens` failure condition with a broader capacity-based fix: it raises `max_num_batched_tokens` to cover the worst-case parallel-draft batch and enlarges the DFlash input buffers. This PR instead leaves the configured target token budget unchanged and caps only synthetic profiling batches to the existing speculator capacity. It covers both the initial skip-attention memory profile and full-attention profiling dummy runs such as FlashInfer autotune, and adds a fail-fast check if a real serving batch violates the scheduler invariant already established by #51256. The approaches are alternatives for the startup crash, but differ in scope and memory/scheduling impact.

#53080 separates target and draft scheduler budgets, but it does not constrain model-runner-generated profiling batches that bypass normal scheduler admission. #53577 covers broader DSpark/PP and padded graph safety work, but it has no matching profile query-buffer cap. #55133 and #56387 address different DSpark failure modes.

## Test Plan

### Common Configuration

- Hardware: 4x NVIDIA H20
- Tensor parallel size: 4
- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:deepseekv41-flash-0909`
- CUDA graph mode: `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`

## Test Result

### DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash

Without this PR, startup fails during memory profiling before the API server becomes ready:

```text
/__w/pytorch/pytorch/aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/IndexKernel.cu:111: operator(): block: [0,0,0], thread: [...] Assertion `-sizes[i] <= index && index < sizes[i] && "index out of bounds"` failed.

Without this PR, startup fails during the initial memory profile. DFlash2 tries to process 128 requests with query width 8, requiring 1024 query rows while its input buffer contains only 512 rows. The logs show:

A 64-concurrency run completed 64/64 requests and generated 2048 completion tokens. [RL][Sleep] Retain frozen weights across level-2 sleep (#57891)

## Purpose

Level-2 sleep discards weights, including frozen parameters omitted by the
trainer. Preserve selected parameters so they remain usable after wake-up
without retransmission.

`sleep_preserve_parameter_names` (CLI: `--sleep-preserve-parameter-names`) matches runtime parameter names
with globs (default: empty; unmatched patterns raise). Selected GPU parameters
are backed up to pageable CPU memory and restored in place on weights wake-up;
CPU-resident parameters need no copy. Backups are released after restoration.
Level-1 behavior is unchanged. The option lives in `ModelConfig` alongside the
other sleep settings and does not require a weight-transfer engine.

Two private Worker methods keep selection and backup state within the sleep/wake lifecycle. XPU inherits the implementation; CPU workers do not support sleep. Selection
covers the target model only. The trainer must omit selected weights, and
reload/post-processing must preserve their values and storage. Budget host
memory for backups; this option does not filter updates.

## Validation

### Focused checks

- Empty selection, CPU-resident parameters, unmatched-pattern rejection,
  in-place restoration, and backup release passed.
- Commit hooks passed, including Ruff and mypy; `git diff --check` passed.

### Real GPU sleep/wake

On an NVIDIA GB200 using the real CuMem sleep backend and a small Llama model:

- Three level-2 cycles retained `lm_head.weight`. All 16,384 bytes and its GPU
  `data_ptr` remained exact after every wake, while a non-retained parameter was
  changed each cycle.
- Level-1 sleep preserved all 180,864 parameter bytes and addresses.
- With the default empty selection, no parameter was backed up and a complete
  reload restored all 180,864 bytes.

Commands run in the pinned serving container:

```bash
python3 /opt/test_frozen_gpu.py configured
python3 /opt/test_frozen_gpu.py empty
```

Both returned `PASS`. After moving the option to `ModelConfig`, the same GPU
tests were rerun with `weight_transfer_config=None`.

The integration results below precede the configuration relocation; the GPU
sleep/wake regression above exercises the current implementation.

### Default VERL update path

An eight-rank run exercised VERL's standard non-layerwise update path. The
trainer omitted four frozen weight/scale tensors per rank. Across all ranks,
32 CPU-resident tensors totaling 202,758,032,400 bytes retained their complete
SHA-256 digest, `data_ptr`, shape, dtype, and device through level-2 sleep and
two updates. All eight trainable shards changed after an optimizer step, and
the subsequent synchronization did not mutate trainer state.

Generation succeeded before and after the update. On the same 30-question
held-out math set, pre/post accuracy was 8/30; all eight non-truncated responses
were correct in both runs. This is integration evidence, not an isolated model
accuracy claim.

### Cross-host TP8

A two-host NVIDIA GB200 test ran TP8 with four ranks per host and default
`FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` CUDA Graphs. Across two real level-2 cycles, the same 32
CPU-resident tensors retained complete SHA-256 digests and addresses both before
and after restoring the other weights. All three generations produced identical
token IDs. There was no OOM and no CUDA Graph invalidation or recapture during
reload.

XPU execution remains untested.

## Duplicate checks

Reviewed #50079 and open sleep/retention PRs. This preserves selected parameters
across level-2 sleep; #55206 releases cached pinned memory and #49789 preserves
post-load runtime state.

AI assistance was used. Human review of the latest revision remains pending.

+#### Retaining frozen weights during RLHF updates
+
+Set `sleep_preserve_parameter_names` (CLI: `--sleep-preserve-parameter-names`)

+patterns for weights that stay frozen during training. Each pattern must match
+`model.named_parameters()`; checkpoint names and `requires_grad` are not used.

+copy. Allow enough host memory for backups. Level-1 behavior is unchanged.
+
+The trainer must omit these parameters from updates, and reload/post-processing
+must preserve their values and storage (including avoiding replacement with meta
+tensors). This option does not filter updates and applies only to the target model.
+
 #### Release only KV cache memory
 
 `LLM.release_kv_cache_memory()` discards KV cache physical memory while keeping model weights resident. It requires a completed pause and all executor memory to be resident: full sleep, partial wake-up, and repeated release without restoring memory are rejected. Requests retained with `mode="keep"` are recomputed after wake-up.

[ROCm][Bugfix] Explicitly reject FSE=1 with DPA+ETP deployment for DeepSeek-V4 (#57919)

## Purpose

Running DeepSeek-V4 on ROCm with data-parallel attention (`--data-parallel-size 8`) and `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1` fails during weight loading with an obscure error.

```bash
File "/.../vllm/vllm/models/deepseek_v4/amd/model.py", line 1243, in load_weights
    param = params_dict[name_mapped]
KeyError: 'layers.0.ffn.experts.routed_experts.w13_weight_scale_inv'
```

Fused shared experts are not supported under data parallelism: the fused path has no way to load the FP8 shared expert into the MXFP4 routed slot, so users end up debugging weight loading instead of the configuration.

This PR fails fast at model construction time: when fused shared experts are requested (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1`), expert parallelism is off, and `data_parallel_size > 1`, the model now raises:

```bash
ValueError: DeepSeek-V4 fused shared experts (VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1) are not supported with data parallelism (data_parallel_size > 1). Set VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=0 to run the shared expert as an unfused FP8 MLP.
```

The check lives in `_fuse_shared_experts_enabled()` in the ROCm-only model file (`vllm/models/deepseek_v4/amd/model.py`), so non-ROCm paths are untouched. Configurations where FSE is already silently disabled (e.g. expert parallelism enabled) do not raise.

## Test Plan

Launch the DPA+ETP server with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1`.

## Test Result

Directly raise `ValueError` so that users know they need to set `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=0` for this scenario, instead of debugging the weight loading code.

---

<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [x] The test plan, such as providing test command.
- [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results
- [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model.
</details>

[Spec Decode] Enable async scheduling for DFlash (#58065)

## Scope

Adds `dflash` to the async-scheduling allowlist in `VllmConfig`, on both the explicit `--async-scheduling` path (previously a hard `ValueError`) and the default auto-enable path (previously force-disabled with a warning). The V2 model runner's async machinery (async output copies, GPU-side draft-token buffers) is method-agnostic, and the DFlash speculator consumes the same GPU tensors (`num_sampled`, `num_rejected`, `last_sampled`) as the DSpark one, so no engine changes beyond the allowlist are needed.


## Configuration

No new configuration. With default settings, async scheduling now stays enabled for `--speculative-config '{"method":"dflash", ...}'` instead of being silently disabled. `--no-async-scheduling` still forces it off.

## Launch command

<details>
<summary>vllm serve command used for validation (GB200, TP4)</summary>

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 -tp 4 \
  --max-num-seqs 32 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --language-model-only \
  --compilation-config '{"pass_config": {"fuse_allreduce_rms": false}}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2","num_speculative_tokens":7,"attention_backend":"TRITON_ATTN"}'
```

(The `fuse_allreduce_rms` workaround is unrelated to this PR: the DFlash2 candidate selector trips a piecewise-compile assert when the allreduce-RMS fusion splits compile ranges at TP4. The TRITON_ATTN draft backend is used because the FLASH_ATTN path is broken for this draft/target pair — FA4-hd256 page-size clash with the hybrid target's mamba-forced KV block size.)

</details>

## Validation

- New unit test `test_dflash_allows_async_scheduling` in `tests/test_config.py`: builds a minimal DFlash2 draft config and asserts async scheduling stays enabled (previously force-disabled). Run: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_config.py -k "dflash or async_scheduling" -q` → 5 passed. `pre-commit run --files vllm/config/vllm.py tests/test_config.py` → all passed (ruff check + format included).
- E2E correctness on 4xGB200 TP4, Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B + z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2 draft (7 speculative tokens, standard rejection, greedy draft, async scheduling on): GSM8K 5-shot flexible-extract 0.9708 / strict-match 0.9704, matching the no-spec baseline 0.9719/0.9716 and the DSpark draft 0.9708/0.9712. Measured acceptance length 5.96 on GSM8K traffic. Repeated with prefix caching enabled (default): 0.9735 / 0.9735 — the hybrid-mamba + prefix-cache + spec-decode path is also correct.

## Performance

Same-build A/B, bs=1 pure-decode (ISL=1, OSL=1000, 2 warmup + 4 requests, `vllm bench serve`, 4xGB200 TP4, DFlash2 with TRITON_ATTN draft backend fully CUDA-graphed, synthetic acceptance length 6):

| async scheduling | TPOT (mean) | decode tok/s |
|---|---|---|
| off (`--no-async-scheduling`) | 2.127 ms | 470.2 |
| on (default with this PR) | 1.510 ms | 662.3 |

**+41% decode throughput (1.41x lower TPOT) at bs=1** with DFlash2 enabled.

## Notes

AI assistance was used for this change (code, tests, and validation); all quoted results were produced by actually running the commands above.

Duplicate-work check: `gh pr list --search "dflash async"` and `gh search prs "async scheduling" "dflash"` over vllm-project/vllm return no open or merged PR enabling async scheduling for DFlash; the allowlist in `vllm/config/vllm.py` on master still excludes it. The sibling DSpark was allowlisted in its original PR (#46995); nothing since covers DFlash.

[Rust Frontend] Add mm-processor benchmark (#51922)

## Summary

- Add a request-scoped multimodal timing registry and RAII stage timers in `vllm-chat`.
- Instrument media fetch, image/video/audio preprocessing, prompt expansion, and total preprocessing time.
- Add a `vllm-bench mm-processor` subcommand that reuses the `random-mm` dataset, supports warmups and concurrency, and reports stage and end-to-end latency statistics (including JSON output).
- Keep timing disabled by default; the benchmark explicitly enables it.

The current benchmark uses a managed headless engine and the full Rust chat pipeline. This is an intentional, documented deviation from a weights-free offline preprocessing-only mode: it provides E2E parity with Python while still isolating preprocessing stages through the new timing hooks. The design document records this tradeoff and the remaining offline-mode question.

## Why this is not duplicate work

Issue #47601 requests reusable Rust-versus-Python preprocessing benchmarks, and maintainers specifically suggested adding a `vllm bench mm-processor`-style CLI. I found no existing PR implementing this Rust benchmark path; this PR supplies the missing timing hooks and benchmark command.

## Testing

- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` — passed
- `cargo fmt --all --check` — passed
- `RUSTFLAGS="-C linker=/usr/bin/gcc" cargo check -p vllm-bench` — passed
- `RUSTFLAGS="-C linker=/usr/bin/gcc" cargo clippy -p vllm-bench --lib -- -D warnings` — passed
- `RUSTFLAGS="-C linker=/usr/bin/gcc" cargo clippy -p vllm-chat --lib -- -D warnings` — passed
- `RUSTFLAGS="-C linker=/usr/bin/gcc" cargo test -p vllm-chat multimodal::timing` — 4 passed, 0 failed
- `RUSTFLAGS="-C linker=/usr/bin/gcc" cargo test -p vllm-bench mm_processor` — test targets compiled successfully; no matching tests were selected
- `.venv/bin/python -m py_compile vllm/benchmarks/mm_processor.py vllm/benchmarks/throughput.py` — passed

The `RUSTFLAGS` linker override is only needed on the ASPIRE2A Cray compiler environment; it bypasses Cray-injected LTO options unsupported by Rust's linker.

No model evaluation is required because this is benchmark tooling only: default request behavior is unchanged and timing collection is opt-in.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for code review, upstream conflict resolution, the managed-engine shutdown fix, validation, and PR description. The human submitter remains responsible for the final end-to-end review and for defending the change with maintainers.

Relates to #47601 and #44280.

commits.message:
[Security] Reject min_tokens that exceeds the filled max_tokens default (#57731)

## Summary
`SamplingParams` skips the `min_tokens <= max_tokens` check while `max_tokens` is unset. The input processor then fills `max_tokens` from `max_model_len` and forwards the request, so an explicit null `max_tokens` with an oversized `min_tokens` is only validated when EngineCore reconstructs the params. That validation error is uncaught on the input-socket thread and wedges the engine. This change re-checks `min_tokens` immediately after filling the default and rejects the request.

## Changes
- `vllm/v1/engine/input_processor.py`: after filling unset `max_tokens`, reject `min_tokens` that exceeds the filled value.
- `tests/test_request_input_bounds.py`: unit coverage for the reject and for an in-range `min_tokens` after fill.
- `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_serving_tokens.py`: generate-endpoint regression for explicit null `max_tokens` plus a follow-up request that must still succeed.

## Codepath coverage
- `/inference/v1/generate`, OpenAI `/v1` generate routes, `/invocations`, offline `LLMEngine` / `AsyncLLM`, and streaming-input adds all go through `InputProcessor.process_inputs`.
- Rust HTTP/gRPC already rejects `min_tokens` above the resolved `max_tokens` in `lower_sampling_params`.

## Duplicate-work check
Searched open and merged PRs for `min_tokens`, `process_input_sockets`, `input_processor max_tokens`, and generate sampling validation.
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54175 bounds a client-supplied `max_tokens` against int32 overflow on the generate route; it does not re-check `min_tokens` after a null `max_tokens` is filled.
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53357 maps `verify()` `ValueError`s to client errors; it does not add this bound.
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55164 validates sampling-param list size limits.
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46733 (merged) is the Rust frontend `min_tokens` check only.

No open or merged PR closes this Python fill-then-forward path.

## Tests
- `test_unset_max_tokens_rejects_oversized_min_tokens` — construction with unset `max_tokens` and oversized `min_tokens` is rejected after fill.
- `test_unset_max_tokens_accepts_min_tokens_within_filled_max` — in-range `min_tokens` still proceeds with the filled default.
- `test_generate_rejects_min_tokens_above_filled_max_tokens` — generate route returns 400 and a later request succeeds.

Commands run:
- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_request_input_bounds.py::test_unset_max_tokens_rejects_oversized_min_tokens tests/test_request_input_bounds.py::test_unset_max_tokens_accepts_min_tokens_within_filled_max tests/test_request_input_bounds.py::test_routed_experts_offset_validated_before_engine_submission -v` — 8 passed
- `.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/engine/input_processor.py tests/test_request_input_bounds.py tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_serving_tokens.py` — passed

The generate-endpoint test was not executed locally (needs a GPU server).

## AI assistance
This PR was developed with AI assistance.

Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

[Bugfix][Frontend] Validate mixed prompt embedding mask lengths (#57006)

## Purpose

Reject a `prompt_is_token_ids` mask whose length differs from the number of prompt embedding rows before submitting the request to the engine.

For example, a Python mixed-embedding prompt with three embedding rows, three token IDs, and a two-element mask currently passes input processing and reaches a NumPy broadcast error in `InputBatch.add_request()`. A one-element mask can instead broadcast silently. The mask describes each prompt position, so both inputs should be rejected at admission.

This adds the check to `InputProcessor` and reports `VLLMValidationError` with `parameter="prompt_is_token_ids"`. Requests without a mask and correctly aligned mixed prompts retain their existing behavior.

I checked related work and did not find an existing fix for this admission check. #54509 fixes mask alignment during truncation; #56656 adds the mask to prefix-cache keys. #51891 touches input validation, but its mask-length condition controls embedding replacement positions and does not reject a mismatched mask.

## Test Plan

The regression tests exercise `InputProcessor.process_inputs()` with empty, short, broadcastable, and long masks. They also cover pure embeddings, token IDs plus embeddings without a mask, and an aligned mixed prompt.

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
  HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/test_request_input_bounds.py \
  tests/renderers/test_chat_utils_prompt_embeds.py \
  tests/v1/engine/test_input_processor_trace_replay.py -q -p no:cacheprovider

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/v1/engine/input_processor.py tests/test_request_input_bounds.py
.venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files \
  vllm/v1/engine/input_processor.py tests/test_request_input_bounds.py
```

## Test Result

- Before the fix, the new cases produced **4 failed, 3 passed**: all four malformed masks were accepted.
- With the fix, the three suites above produced **123 passed**.
- All applicable pre-commit hooks and the manual mypy 3.12 check passed.
- A10 / Qwen3.5-0.8B (BF16, eager, prefix caching disabled): the baseline legacy runner reproduced the broadcast error; the next normal request returned `EngineDeadError` as well.
- With the fix, the legacy and V2 runners each passed **11 checks**: three valid generation controls, four rejected mask lengths (0, 1, 2, 4), and successful normal generation after each rejection. The valid controls produced the same token IDs before/after the fix and across runners.

[Bugfix][Qwen2.5-VL] Honor video fps for temporal M-RoPE (#47736)

## Purpose

Qwen2.5-VL currently loses video metadata before calling the HuggingFace processor. Since the HF video processor refactor, `second_per_grid_ts` is computed from `video_metadata.sampled_fps`; when vLLM drops that metadata, pre-decoded videos fall back to a default sampled fps instead of the request/video fps. That value drives the temporal M-RoPE scale used by the model, so videos tagged at 1fps and 30fps get the same temporal spacing in vLLM.

This fixes the Qwen2.5-VL path by keeping video metadata in the data parser, splitting `(video, metadata)` tuples before the HF processor call, and forwarding `video_metadata` so HF can compute `sampled_fps` from the real frame metadata. The dummy video builder also attaches synthetic metadata, matching the Qwen3-VL pattern and keeping memory profiling inputs valid once metadata is required.

Scope: the Qwen2.5-VL processor path. Qwen2-VL does not capture `second_per_grid_ts` in the same way, so that would be a separate change. vLLM's video loader already attaches metadata for URL/file inputs; the changed behavior is that bare pre-decoded video arrays without metadata now fail clearly instead of silently using a fallback fps.

Duplicate-work check: I did not find an open PR covering Qwen2.5-VL video metadata forwarding. PR #23058 is Qwen2.5-Omni only, PR #43198 only lets video frame sampling use a request `fps` override, PR #45555 only adds loader-side metadata that this path still dropped, and PR #47407 only bounds M-RoPE positions.

## Test Plan

Run a real `Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct` `LLM.generate` path on an RTX 4090, instrument the live model's `iter_mm_grid_thw`, and compare the temporal `t_factor` for the same video tagged as fps=1.0 and fps=30.0 before, after, and after reverting the fix. Add one CPU regression case to the existing Qwen2-VL processor test file to assert `second_per_grid_ts` tracks fps, run affected Qwen2.5-VL video tests, and run ruff on all changed files.

## Test Result

Upstream main commit `e433634c781dce7ee55563424b8136ad3495c1be` before the fix, same video at two fps values:

| input fps | t_factor |
|---:|---:|
| 1.0 | 0.1669921875 |
| 30.0 | 0.1669921875 |

After the fix:

| input fps | t_factor |
|---:|---:|
| 1.0 | 4.0 |
| 30.0 | 0.1337890625 |

Reverting the patch restored the before behavior:

| input fps | t_factor |
|---:|---:|
| 1.0 | 0.1669921875 |
| 30.0 | 0.1669921875 |

[Rust Frontend] Build full-output grammars from initialized reasoning parsers (#57340)

## Purpose

Strict tool grammars currently start after the engine detects the end of reasoning. This change builds the reasoning phase from the initialized Rust parser and composes it with the visible-output grammar, allowing XGrammar to constrain the generated stream from token zero.

Step 2, following the merged #55269. That PR introduces the parser-owned grammar interfaces and request lifecycle; this follow-up activates `FromTokenZero` coverage for supported delimited reasoning parsers. The open-PR search found no separate implementation of this layer.

- Build the reasoning continuation from the final prompt state, including model-specific closing separators and any separator suffix remaining after prompt prefill.
- Enable the wrapper for DeepSeek R1/V3, Qwen3, GLM45, Step3/Step3.5, Nemotron V3, and HY3/HY4 through their existing parser implementations and aliases.
- Project the MiniMax M2 builder to its visible-output grammar before composing the reasoning wrapper, with an explicit check of the expected builder prefix.
- Preserve the existing tool-grammar activation policy. Supported requests use `reasoning_ended = Some(true)` through Step 1's lowering; the grammar requires the reasoning close before entering visible output.

K3, Gemma4, Inkling, and Harmony remain follow-up work.

## Test Plan

The builder-parity invariant is:

```text
reasoning-wrapped visible tool tag = builder output with the matching reasoning mode
```

`assert_builder_parity` checks 54 cases: nine reasoning/tool parser pairs × `ReasoningMode::{Enabled, Auto}` × required/named/strict-auto tool choices. Enabled initializes inside a prefilled reasoning block; Auto initializes without a reasoning boundary. Every case asserts `FromTokenZero` coverage. The comparison flattens nested sequences and ignores `AnyText.excludes`, including inside `Optional`, while retaining token and character budgets. It checks normalized grammar structure.

## Test Result

- After restacking onto main with #55269 merged: **1513 parser/chat/text/server/LLM/engine-client tests passed, 1 skipped**, including production renderer/parser roundtrips; XGrammar structural tags 0.3.0.
- Auto parity was confirmed failing before extending normalization into `Optional`, then all **54 cases passed** with the recursive normalization.
- Strict Clippy, formatting, and diff checks passed.
- Earlier local XGrammar 0.2.7 validation: 18 HY3/HY4 grammar configurations passed 72 token-mask/acceptance/stop replays with a controlled vocabulary; 9 HY3 configurations passed 36 replays with its cached model tokenizer.
### Prior GPU end-to-end regression checks

Paired GB200 runs on September 17–18 compared Step 1 [`ef67e07c`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/ef67e07c686c0e758815701d239a28e48da1e169) with Step 2 [`b38299c9`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/b38299c9fa958ac1471a77455969868457153d4b), using the same checkpoint, requests, and serving settings within each pair. The following model/parser configurations had **zero candidate-only task failures in the evaluated samples**. Success requires the expected answer and tool/direct-text behavior, with completion within the output budget. Counts show Step 1 → Step 2; existing failures remain included.

| Model family / tested checkpoint | Reasoning parser | Tool / unified parser | Paired GPU e2e result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3: Qwen3-4B | `qwen3` | `qwen3_xml` | Native tasks 33/33 → 33/33; GSM8K 14/16 → 15/16; explicit starting states 21/21 → 21/21 |
| Qwen3.5: Qwen3.5-4B | `qwen3` | `qwen3_coder` | Native tasks 33/33 → 33/33; GSM8K 15/16 → 16/16; explicit starting states 21/21 → 21/21 |
| Qwen3.5: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8 | `qwen3` | `qwen3_coder` | Native tasks 33/33 → 33/33; GSM8K 15/16 → 16/16; explicit starting states 21/21 → 21/21 |
| GLM4.7: GLM-4.7-Flash | `glm47` | `glm47` | Native tasks 27/33 → 29/33; GSM8K 13/16 → 13/16; explicit starting states 11/12 → 11/12 |
| DeepSeek V4: DeepSeek-V4-Flash | `deepseek_v4` | `deepseek_v4` | Native tasks 33/33 → 33/33; GSM8K 15/16 → 15/16; explicit starting states 11/12 → 11/12 |
| DeepSeek V3.2: DeepSeek-V3.2 | `deepseek_v3` | `deepseek_v32` | Combined semantic suite 112/117 → 112/117; identical five failed cases |
| DeepSeek V4.1: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash | `deepseek_v41` | `deepseek_v41` | Combined semantic suite 114/117 → 115/117 |
| HY4: Hy4-preview-FP8 | Unified parser | `hy_v4` (selected by `auto`) | Combined semantic suite 111/117 → 111/117; identical six failed cases |

Coverage includes required/named/strict-auto tool choice, reasoning modes and prompt-derived starting states, streaming, quoted reasoning delimiters, direct answers, sampled generation, a 16-question GSM8K sample, and real three-turn tool conversations. All listed checkpoints completed the three-turn flow 3/3 in both arms. The combined semantic suites exclude a separate deliberately insufficient 16-token truncation probe. HY4 baseline requests span restarted batches after Slurm preemption, with frozen model and request settings.

The broader campaign also found stable synthetic-prefix regressions in R1-Distill and Nemotron, and unresolved semantic differences in HY3 and GLM5.3; those configurations require follow-up. These results provide bounded evidence for the listed checkpoints and tested commits. **GPU revalidation of the current rebased head remains pending.**
